input_vector.representation: Raw board features are concatenated in the segment order below, then normalized per column using feature_means and feature_stdevs saved in each checkpoint. If a standard deviation is zero, that feature is left unscaled.
input_vector.padding_note: The feature function determines thrown/not_thrown from the input SheetStates array width. If a caller pads SheetStates to num_stones before feature construction (as self-play does), every column is marked thrown and zero coordinates are processed as coordinates.

segments.name: first_team
segments.meaning: Team ID (0 or 1) assigned to the first stone slot; subsequent stone-slot teams alternate.

segments.name: not_thrown
segments.meaning: 1 for a column added by the feature function when extending a narrower SheetStates array to num_stones; otherwise 0.

segments.name: thrown
segments.meaning: 1 for each column already present in the input SheetStates array; otherwise 0. This reflects array width, not whether a stone remains in play.

segments.name: x
segments.meaning: Stone-slot x coordinates in metres. Columns added by the feature function are 0; upstream padding remains a 0 coordinate.

segments.name: y
segments.meaning: Stone-slot y coordinates in metres. Columns added by the feature function are 0; upstream padding remains a 0 coordinate.

segments.name: distance_from_house_center
segments.meaning: Radial distance from the house center in metres. It is 0 for columns added by the feature function; upstream zero coordinates also have distance 0.

segments.name: in_house
segments.meaning: 1 when the column's distance is less than house_outer_circle_radius + stone_radius, otherwise 0. Columns added by the feature function are 0; an upstream zero-coordinate column is evaluated at the house center and is 1.

output_vector.representation: Unnormalized class logits. Applying softmax gives the predicted probability for each final net score from the first team's perspective.
output_vector.class_index_to_net_score: column j represents net score j - num_stones_per_side, for j from 0 through 2 * num_stones_per_side. Positive scores favor the first team; negative scores favor the other team.
output_vector.training_target: One-hot vector for the observed final net score.

description: Model checkpoints only. Training datasets and physics caches are stored outside weights/. Each checkpoint is a NumPy NPZ archive.
